text:
Yes, there is a tree-cover loss candidate, but it is not yet corroborated.

Hansen GFC (v1.13) shows a 13.5 ha tree-cover loss event in 2025, about 3.9% of the 345.6 ha property. JRC's 2020 forest map agrees with it at 0.98, and the surrounding area is native forest context. JRC shows about 227 ha (65.7%) of the property as forest in 2020.

Caveats:
- 2025 is the latest year in the series, so we can't yet tell whether the loss persists. The corroboration rule requires a later observed year, so the event stays "pending corroboration."
- Hansen loss means any stand replacement, so this doesn't show deforestation or a land-use change. It could be, for example, harvest of a plantation.
- The evidence doesn't give the cause (harvest, fire, storm, clearing) or whether it was legal or authorized.
- It supports no compliance finding, such as EUDR status.

The MGAP 2021 source was not available.
